newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul suffers worst terror since Taleban arrival.
newsitem.headline: Kabul suffers worst terror since Taleban arrival.

text.p: An air raid and bomb blast has made Sunday the Afghan capital's blackest day since the purist Islamic Taleban took over the city in late September last year.
The two attacks killed at least eight people and wounded 52, witnesses said on Monday. Local hospitals said they had admitted 40 casualties from the blasts.
Taleban fighters blamed the forces of the opposition alliance of forces loyal to the ousted government of president Burhanuddin Rabbani and their ally General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
The front line is some 40 km (25 miles) north of Kabul and in the remote northwestern provinces of Afghanistan.
"The infidels and the corrupt elements of Dostum are responsible for these attacks," said Taleban guard Sher Patcha at Kabul's busiest vegetable market, the site of the bomb blast.
There have been no claims of responsibility and no comment from the Dostum alliance.
After a lull of more than a month, there have been seven air raids on Kabul since December 28, when the Taleban launched an offensive north of Kabul and pushed the opposition back 10 km (six miles).
In Sunday's air raid, two planes dropped eight bombs on residential areas in the northeast of the city, witnesses said.
The bombs killed at least four people according to local residents, and the nearby hospital said it had admitted 15 people. The raid also destroyed three houses.
A bomb exploded in Kabul's busiest vegetable market in the early evening on Sunday.
"Just after four o'clock there was a huge explosion," guard Sher Patcha said. "Four people were killed and 37 wounded."
Aminullah, a trader who sells carrots at the market, said the area soon filled with smoke.
"Everyone was running. Women were taking cover in shops. No one knew what was happening," he said.
"When the smoke cleared we could see many wounded and dead, I could not count them all. All the victims were traders and poor people."
The Taleban captured Kabul in September and now control more than two-thirds of Afghanistan. They are enforcing a strict Islamic code.
